claims.text: Query perturbation combined with consistency score calculation can identify potential LLM hallucination scenarios without relying on context or ground truth.
GPT-4 hallucinates the least among evaluated foundation models when subjected to query perturbations.
Non-GPT-4 foundation models begin hallucinating when exposed to minor character-level perturbations such as typos.

evidence.description: The authors present a framework relying on query perturbation and consistency score calculation between original and perturbed query responses, operating without context or ground truth.
Experimental evaluation demonstrates that GPT-4 hallucinates the least when faced with perturbations across tested foundation models.
Experimental evaluation shows that other LLMs start hallucinating even when presented with minor typos.

methodologies.name: Query perturbation and consistency scoring framework
methodologies.description: A framework evaluating LLM response consistency across character-level, word-level, and sentence-level query perturbations to detect hallucination scenarios without reference context or ground truth.
conditions: absence of context and ground truth

limitations.text: Detecting hallucinations using context or golden responses becomes challenging post-deployment where both context and ground truth are typically absent.
